```sh
du -sh /home/user | awk '{print $1}'
```

This command uses `du` to display the size of each file in the `/home/user` directory and `awk` to extract only the file sizes.

```sh
find . -type f -name "*.swift" -exec grep -n {} {} + | wc -l
```

This command uses `find` to locate all Swift files (`*.swift`) in the current directory and its subdirectories. It then uses `grep` to search each file for lines

```sh
du -sh .
```

This command uses the `du` command to display the disk usage of each file and directory in the current directory. The `-sh` option sorts the output by size in descending order.

```sh
for f in *.txt; do
  echo "Replacing '$f' with '$f' in '$f'"
done
```

This command iterates over all `.txt` files in the current directory and replaces each file with itself.

```sh
git reset HEAD~1
```

This command resets the current branch to the commit before the last one, effectively undoing the last commit but keeping the changes.

```sh
grep -r TODO /path/to/javascript/files -v node_modules
```

This command searches for the string "TODO" in all JavaScript files located in the specified directory (`/path/to/javascript/files`) and excludes any files that contain the string "node_modules".
